theory.title: Phrasal verbs de viaje y objetos separables
theory.explanation: Los phrasal verbs combinan un verbo con una partícula y suelen tener un significado propio. Aprende combinaciones frecuentes de viaje como set off (salir), check in (facturar/registrarse), get on (subir), get off (bajar), look around (explorar) y run out of (quedarse sin). Con los separables, el pronombre suele ir entre el verbo y la partícula: pick it up (recógelo).
theory.tip: Aprende cada phrasal verb dentro de una frase y observa dónde va el objeto.

content.passage: Our coach set off late because one passenger had not checked in on time. We got on at the central station and got off near the harbour. Unfortunately, the driver realised that the coach was running out of fuel, so he dropped us off at a service area. While we waited, we looked around the shops and found out that another coach would arrive in twenty minutes. In the end, we reached the hotel safely.

items.prompt: Describe a time you set off early for a journey.
items.modelAnswer: I set off early for a journey to the airport because I knew the motorway could be busy. The roads were quiet, and I arrived with enough time to have breakfast before checking in. It made the start of the trip much calmer.

items.prompt: Explain how to check in for a flight.
items.modelAnswer: To check in for a flight, I go to the airline's desk or use the online service before arriving. I show my passport if required, drop off my suitcase and check the departure gate. I keep my boarding pass easy to find.

items.prompt: Which kind of transport do you get on most often?
items.modelAnswer: I get on the train most often because it takes me to work without traffic. I can read or listen to music during the journey. If I need to travel locally, I sometimes get on a bus instead.

items.prompt: Talk about getting off at the wrong stop.
items.modelAnswer: Once I got off at the wrong stop because I was reading a message and missed the announcement. I checked the route, walked to the next stop and took a bus in the opposite direction. Now I pay more attention.

items.prompt: Recommend a place to look around in your town.
items.modelAnswer: I recommend looking around the old market area in my town. There are small independent shops, a historic church and several cafés. It is easy to explore on foot and gives visitors a good idea of local life.

items.prompt: What would you do if your car ran out of fuel?
items.modelAnswer: If my car ran out of fuel, I would move it to a safe place if possible and turn on the hazard lights. I would call roadside assistance and avoid walking along a busy road. In future, I would refuel earlier.

items.prompt: Describe something you need to pick up before travelling.
items.modelAnswer: Before travelling, I usually pick up a few snacks, a bottle of water and any tickets I have printed. If I am going abroad, I also collect the currency I need. I prefer doing these jobs the day before.

items.prompt: Have you experienced a cancellation or a service being called off?
items.modelAnswer: I experienced a train cancellation during a winter storm. The railway company called off the service and offered a replacement bus. I checked the updated information and told the person waiting for me that I would be late.

items.prompt: Talk about a time someone dropped you off somewhere.
items.modelAnswer: A friend dropped me off at the airport early one morning. He helped me unload my suitcase and waited until I had found the correct entrance. It was kind of him because the weather was very cold.

items.prompt: Explain how you find out about travel delays.
items.modelAnswer: I check travel delays using the transport company's app and the information screens at the station. If the delay is serious, I look for another route and contact anyone who is expecting me.

A: Yes, and we have printed the tickets. B: Which station will you use? A: The central one. B: Is there a local guide? A: Yes, we made a booking online. B: Do you know the platform? A: It is shown on the app. B: What will you visit? A: The museum and the market. B: Are you learning about local customs? A: Yes, and we are staying at a small hotel. B: Enjoy your arrival!
